Simulate the raw impacts that studies would report

Source: R/simulate.R
simulate_raw_impacts.Rd

For validation: given a population whose disease combinations follow the maximum-entropy distribution of model (see fit_joint()), and known true additive impacts (and optional interactions), computes what a study would estimate for each impact row: the crude difference between the two groups the row compares, or the regression coefficient of an adjusted row (see cm_impacts() for what a row means). With n = NULL the exact population values are returned; with n set, n animals are sampled, which adds sampling error.

Usage

simulate_raw_impacts(
  model,
  true_impacts,
  interactions = NULL,
  rows = NULL,
  adjusted_for = NA_character_,
  n = NULL,
  joint = NULL,
  units = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

model

A cm_population() or cm_model() (its impacts are ignored).

true_impacts

Named numeric vector of true impacts, one per disease (any units).

interactions

Optional named numeric vector of true interactions, named by combination (e.g. c("d1;d2" = 0.5)), in the same units.

rows

Optional data frame of the rows to simulate, with column disease and optional among and adjusted_for. Default: one row per disease (with adjusted_for) and one crude row per interaction.

adjusted_for

For the default rows: adjustment sets (ids separated by ";", or "all"), one per disease or recycled.

n

Optional number of animals to sample.

joint

Optional pre-computed fit_joint() result. It must match the model and have converged; a joint fitted here that does not converge stops with class deconflate_nonconvergence.

units

Optional units label for the returned impacts.

...

Not used (arguments of earlier versions give a message).

Value

A cm_impacts() object with the simulated raw impacts.

Details

Adjusting the returned raw impacts with deconflate() recovers true_impacts and interactions exactly (for n = NULL), whenever the rows determine them.

Examples

raw <- simulate_raw_impacts(example_supplement(), c(d1 = 2, d2 = 4, d3 = 6),
                            interactions = c("d1;d2" = 1))
raw
#>   row disease among adjusted_for measure    value study               source
#> 1   1      d1  <NA>         <NA>    <NA> 2.666100  <NA> simulated (expected)
#> 2   2      d2  <NA>         <NA>    <NA> 5.569634  <NA> simulated (expected)
#> 3   3      d3  <NA>         <NA>    <NA> 6.691225  <NA> simulated (expected)
#> 4   4   d1;d2  <NA>         <NA>    <NA> 8.082420  <NA> simulated (expected)
#>   note
#> 1 <NA>
#> 2 <NA>
#> 3 <NA>
#> 4 <NA>
deconflate(cm_model(example_supplement(), raw))$adjusted
#>   disease        kind      raw adjusted     change rows
#> 1      d1     disease 2.666100        2 -0.2498407    1
#> 2      d2     disease 5.569634        4 -0.2818199    1
#> 3      d3     disease 6.691225        6 -0.1033032    1
#> 4   d1;d2 interaction 8.082420        1         NA    1
